description: Issue summary: Customer reports streaming SSE endpoint returns HTTP 200 but final JSON array is truncated (missing closing bracket) when an upstream connection rebind/redirect happens during worker draining. Impact: AtlasHealth's chat UI displays a partial JSON body and the client never receives the terminal end-event; users must refresh to get a retry. Observed behavior: 1) Server responds 200 immediately and then stream ends with EOF before closing the JSON array. 2) Edge logs show an upstream 302 redirect from A/B redirector during the final token window. 3) Resume attempts from client result in a resumed stream that duplicates earlier segments or returns an empty array depending on timing.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a long-running SSE generation session in prod-us-east against redwood-v1-medium with typical prompt length (>= 600 tokens).
2) Trigger a canary redirect at the edge (simulate A/B redirector returning 302 for the session cookie) while the model is streaming its final paragraph (within last 2-5s).
3) Observe client receives HTTP 200, a partial JSON array (missing trailing "]"), then EOF without terminal end-event.
4) Attempt a resume: client reconnects with resume_token; server either duplicates prefix segments or returns an empty array and final marker is missing.

comments: 2026-03-10 15:01 - Support (Maya Thompson): Notified customer and requested HAR/HTTP trace. Asked for reproduction steps and browser/SDK version.
2026-03-10 16:22 - Customer (AtlasHealth - Jake R.): Provided browser network trace and confirmed this started after they enabled a phased redirect experiment on their CDN.

2026-03-11 09:08 - Eng (Riley Chen): Reproduced locally with a scripted redirect; captured identical truncated JSON array and missing terminal end-event. Assigned to Edge team to inspect redirect/in-flight drain interactions.

2026-03-12 11:47 - Edge (Lucas Meyer): Edge rewrite layer (ab-router) was injecting a 302 to rebind session which sometimes causes upstream to half-close connection before final chunk flush; investigating mitigation.
2026-03-12 16:10 - Support (Aisha Patel): Advised AtlasHealth temporary workaround: disable canary redirect for streaming routes or enable websocket fallback in their integration.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Edge 302 during in-flight stream causes upstream worker to start drain sequence; worker sends FIN before internal flush ensures final marker is emitted. This yields HTTP 200 with incomplete body.

Hypothesis B: The redirect sets a cookie which changes session affinity; resume_token mapping uses sticky session id that is reused for another recent session leading to offset collision and duplication on resume.
Observed: Upstream generator service does write final choice but connection close occurs between chunking and chunk flush to socket (timing window ~80-140ms).
Trace: tcpdump shows FIN after last write but before kernel send buffers drained; edge returns 200 because headers already sent.
resolution_notes: Short term workaround provided to customer: disable the A/B redirect for SSE endpoints or switch to websocket mode to avoid HTTP redirect semantics; also suggested client-side retry logic that treats incomplete JSON as transient and re-requests completion.

Mitigation being developed: Edge patch to transform in-flight 302 into a grace-aware redirect for streaming paths: if a streaming response is in progress, delay redirect until final-marker flush or instead inject a 307 upgrade hint to preserve connection until generator confirms terminal event.

Server-side patch: generator will ensure an explicit "END_EVENT" sentinel is emitted and flushed with a blocking write prior to initiating graceful drain. Patch PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/899

Follow-up actions: 1) Edge team to land canary for ab-router patch (PR referenced above). 2) Add monitoring for truncated JSON arrays on streaming endpoints and alert at >0.1% rate. 3) Update SSE resume logic to validate resume_token epoch and refuse non-monotonic offsets (prevents duplication).
Status: Mitigations in review (edge patch + generator flush). Customer workaround in place; monitoring and alerts planned.
resolution: Mitigations in review; customer has temporary workaround (disable redirect or use websocket fallback). Edge + serving-runtime patches pending review and canary.
